title: Tenant fallback braid and integrity brief
summary: Draft customer-facing summary covering a multi-stage service disruption caused by an unexpected interaction between regional router updates and new model-variant fallbacks. Provides a short statuspage-ready blurb, a plain-language postmortem for customers, recommended actions for tenants, and verification steps to confirm data integrity. Emphasis on practical mitigations (idempotency keys, client-side de-dup, replay windows) rather than deep internal telemetry.
intended_audience: Affected customers, account teams, and partner integrators that observed transient duplicate or mis-ordered completions during the incident window.
statuspage_update_draft: We experienced a partial service disruption for multi-region model routing between 2029-03-14 18:12 UTC and 2029-03-15 02:07 UTC that may have caused duplicate responses, short-lived mis-ordering of streaming chunks, and elevated latency for a subset of tenant requests. Impact: customers in eu-west and us-central regions with model-fallthrough enabled. Mitigation: traffic has been routed to stable variants and we have completed a staged rollback of the recent routing rule. The platform is currently stable; no ongoing degradation detected. We are validating cached response integrity and will post a full customer summary and recommended replay steps by 2029-03-18 20:00 UTC. If you see persistent issues after that time, please open a priority support ticket.
postmortem_customer_summary: What happened: A routing rollout introduced a braid of fallback rules intended to gracefully degrade to smaller model variants. Under a narrow concurrency pattern and an unexpected interaction with KV cache invalidation, the router occasionally returned duplicate routed requests to downstream workers. This produced duplicate completions for some idempotent-less workloads and transient reordering for streaming sessions. Why it mattered: Customer applications that do not include idempotency keys or dedup logic could see repeated outputs or short bursts of extra token charges. What we did: - immediate mitigation: paused the rollout and rerouted affected regions to pinned stable variants within 33 minutes of first alerts - operational fix: applied a coordination mutex in router code to prevent parallel fallback decisions from emitting duplicate downstream requests - validation: ran an integrity verification job comparing request ids, checksums of completions, and KV cache state across replicas - scope: estimated 0.6% of requests in affected regions during the window were impacted (we captured sampling traces to identify tenant-level exposure). Data safety: No customer training data or stored documents were modified. All outputs are transient model responses; we verified there were no writes to durable stores as part of the failure path.
next_steps_and_customer_actions: 1) Check for duplicate outputs: If your integration lacks idempotency keys, search recent traces for identical response bodies within 30s windows. 2) Recommended short-term client changes: - Add/request idempotency keys for generation calls where dedup matters - For streaming: implement monotonic chunk sequencing to reassemble reliably - For batched/reranked requests: run a local checksum (e.g., sha256) and ignore exact duplicates during incident windows 3) Replay guidance: We offer two replay paths depending on your needs: - Safe replay (non-destructive): re-run requests against the pinned stable variant with request ids preserved; this will not modify customer data and is suitable for read-only flows - Full re-evaluation: for workflows that depend on ephemeral completion ordering, we can coordinate a controlled replay with our Solutions team. To request replay assistance, include sample request ids and the time window in your support ticket. 4) SLA and credits: If you identify measurable consumer impact tied to duplicate billing or sustained latency within the window, contact your account team; we will validate and process appropriate credits per your contract. 5) Verification checklist we ran: - cross-region checksum comparison - KV cache eviction logs inspection - per-tenant sampled trace reconciliation
verification_and_integrity_checks: We ran the following verification steps and are sharing them for customer audits: (A) Request -> response idempotence map: matched request ids to responses and flagged duplicates. (B) Response checksum diff: computed sha256 across completions captured by the ingress tracer, looked for identical blobs indicating duplication. (C) KV cache timeline: validated cache invalidations did not persist beyond the incident TTL and that no stale fragments were served after 02:07 UTC. (D) Durable-store audit: confirmed no persistent writes happened during the failure path. Results: sample-based checks indicate duplication only within the incident window; no persisted customer data corruption. If you would like the sampled trace package for your tenant, request it via your support ticket (we will redact non-customer traces as needed).
contact_and_escalation: Primary contact: Aisha Patel (customer-success lead) — aisha@redwood.ai. Technical on-call: eng-oncall@redwood.ai (24/7). For priority escalations please mention JIRA-INC-4837 and tag @solutions-team in the partner Slack channel #cs-solutions. Account reps: reach out to your named rep for SLA/credit conversations.
notes_and_open_questions: - We are proposing to add a router-level test that simulates concurrent fallback decisions; tracking PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2891 - Open item: automated tenant notification for future routing rollouts that touch pinned variants — product/console team to propose UI copy by 2029-03-22 - Consider offering an SDK helper for idempotency key generation and client-side dedup templates (owner: devexp)
actions_and_timeline: Completed: paused rollout (2029-03-14 18:45 UTC), pinned variants (18:55 UTC), applied code mutex (2029-03-14 21:10 UTC), validation job completed (2029-03-15 02:07 UTC). Planned: SDK helper RFC (due 2029-03-22), console rollout-notice UX (draft due 2029-03-20), customer replay assistance window opens 2029-03-18 09:00 UTC and closes 2029-04-01 23:59 UTC.
